Playbook.name: Host — Mass File Change Burst (Possible Ransomware or Destruction) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One host had a burst of file changes (>=100 distinct files created/updated/moved/deleted via FIM in the window; 24h/host suppressed). Triage: active ransomware/destruction, or a legitimate bulk operation (backup/migration/software update)?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A mass file-change burst is the signature of ransomware encryption or destructive wiping.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows FIM (verified live; monitors Windows system paths). Fields: file.path, file.name, file.extension, event.action, host.name.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the mass file-change burst is ransomware/destruction or a legitimate bulk operation.

Step.name: File-change burst profile
Step.Purpose: The action mix and file extensions distinguish encryption (renames/new extensions) from a benign bulk write.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE event.dataset == "fim.event" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND event.action IN ("created","updated","moved","deleted") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS files = COUNT_DISTINCT(file.path), creates = COUNT(CASE(event.action=="created",1,null)), renames = COUNT(CASE(event.action=="moved",1,null)), deletes = COUNT(CASE(event.action=="deleted",1,null)), extensions = VALUES(file.extension) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: High renames/deletes with new uniform extensions (.locked, random) = ransomware encryption. High creates of a known type by a backup/migration = benign. Mass deletes = possible wiping. Read the extensions.

Step.name: What is driving the changes (ransom notes / process)
Step.Purpose: Ransom-note files or a specific driving process confirm ransomware vs a bulk job.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE event.dataset == "fim.event" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND event.action == "created" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE file.name RLIKE "(?i).*(readme|decrypt|recover|restore|lock).*" | STATS ransom_notes = COUNT(*), names = VALUES(file.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Ransom-note-style files created during the burst confirm ransomware - isolate immediately. None + a known bulk operation supports benign.

Node.Condition: High renames/deletes with new extensions, or ransom-note files created during the burst.
Node.Result: True Positive (Ransomware/Destruction - ISOLATE host NOW, activate IR)

Node.Condition: A legitimate bulk operation (backup/migration/update) with a known driver, no ransom notes.
A misconfigured job mass-changing files benignly.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FIM-BURST, INV-02-FIM-CAUSE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the operation; close as benign_activity.
Isolate the host immediately; activate ransomware IR; protect backups; scope the spread; identify patient zero.
Fix the job; document; tune the rule.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Assess the change pattern; if ransomware, ISOLATE the host immediately.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; activate ransomware IR; protect backups; scope spread.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Ensure backups/immutability; EDR ransomware protection; segment file shares.

QualityChecks.Check: 24h/host suppressed; fim.event monitors Windows paths. Correlate with Sysmon process for the driver.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Ransomware contained; spread scoped; backups verified.
